subject: English_grammar
text:
This is Asma Ahmed’s bed room. The room is very neatly made. It has a bed
with pillows, cushions, and a colorful, flowery bed-cover. There’s a rug in front
of the bed with another big cushion. An excellent painting of the sea is hanging
from the wall while another small painting is kept on the top of the right
side-table. The room has a rocking chair and a sofa at the left corner. The
windows are covered with large heavy curtain. Can you see a mask somewhere
around the bed?

subject: English_grammar
text:
The bold words in the passage are examples of articles in English. Can you
find out any principle or rule about the use of a, an and the in the passage ?
English Grammar and Composition 41
Use of articles
1.
We use a/an to talk about something for the first time.
e.g. a bed, a bed-cover, a rug, a rocking chair, a sofa, a mask

subject: English_grammar
text:
In the text above, when the speaker uses any singular countable noun,
s/he uses either a or an before it.
We also use a/an to refer to something unspecified, e.g. not particular
or specific.
She bought some apples from a shop in the new market. In this sentence
the shop in the new market is not specific as there are many shops in the
new market. So, article has been used before it.

subject: English_grammar
text:
‘A’ is used before consonants and ‘an’ is used before vowel.
‘A’ is used before vowel ‘U’ when it is pronounced as ‘you’. So, we have to use
‘a’ before university, but not ‘an’ before university.
‘An’ is used before consonant if the first ‘h’ of a word is silent: an hour, an
honest man etc.
We use the when we refer to something for the second time.

subject: English_grammar
text:
e.g. This is Asma Ahmed’s bed room. The room is very neatly made.
(room:1* time) (room: 2"¢ time)
We use the when we refer to any person or object specifically.
e.g. There are few windows in the room. The windows are covered with
large heavy curtain.

subject: English_grammar
text:
In the second sentence, the windows are specific in the sentence: which
windows the speaker is referring to. The windows are the windows of
Asma Ahmed.
We also use the to refer to something that has no alternative.
e.g. The sun is the source of energy in the earth.
